guard: An effect failure that crosses the version-2 entry's thread boundary keeps its whole domain: the driver rehydrates code+kind back into the EffectError the walker would have raised in-process, so failure handling downstream branches on the same fields either way.
proveWith: pnpm mutation-proof --config implementations/runtime/smoke/mutations/engine-host-domain.json   # --config resolves against the repo root, never the cwd

mutations.name: an effect failure crosses the driver boundary stripped of its domain
mutations.expectRed: and the effect FAILS rather than returning a resolved checkpoint with an empty value
mutations.cell: and the effect FAILS rather than returning a resolved checkpoint with an empty value
mutations.note: The cell reads `kind === "handler-fault"` off the raised failure, which is exactly the field this branch restores. Mutated, a bypassed checkpoint's L4000 arrives as a plain error with a code and no kind, and a caller that branches on the domain - as this suite does on the walker's own raise - reads a different failure than the one that happened. Found live before the branch existed: this cell was the red that demanded it.

why: One mutation, its own config, because the observing cell lives in a different suite than the
rest of the engine-host guards: mesh-checkpoint is where a real handler throw crosses the
boundary with a kind a cell actually reads.
